articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft patches a whopping 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. Meanwhile Chrome users get their fourth helping of patches this year — bon appétit, security theater lovers.

articles.title: Silver Fox Springs Tax-Themed Attacks on Orgs in India, Russia
articles.summary: Critical cPanel authentication bypass flaw gets the full exploit circus treatment after disclosure, with researchers claiming zero-day activity for at least a month. When your web hosting control panel becomes a public playground, you know someone's having a bad day.

articles.title: We Scanned 1 Million Exposed AI Services. Here's How Bad the Security Actually Is
articles.summary: MetInfo CMS gets absolutely wrecked by CVE-2026-29014, a critical code injection flaw with a perfect 9.8 CVSS score. Open-source content management just became open-season remote code execution.

articles.title: Securing the Agentic Workforce: Cisco Announces Intent to Acquire Astrix Security
articles.summary: Weaver E-cology platform suffers critical RCE via debug API exploitation, proving once again that leaving debug endpoints in production is like handing attackers the keys to the kingdom. CVSS 9.8 says it all.

articles.title: CISA says ‘Copy Fail’ flaw now exploited to root Linux systems
articles.summary: Progress Software's MOVEit Automation gets hit with another critical auth bypass vulnerability. Because apparently the first time MOVEit got pwned wasn't educational enough for everyone involved.

articles.title: Claude Security enters public beta with Opus 4.7 vulnerability scanning and patching
articles.summary: CISA confirms 'Copy Fail' Linux vulnerability is being actively exploited just one day after researchers dropped a PoC. The time between disclosure and exploitation keeps shrinking faster than our collective faith in responsible disclosure.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and aggravated identity theft for text-message phishing attacks. Another young Brit learns that cybercrime doesn't pay — at least not when you get caught.

articles.title: EFF and 18 Organizations Urge UK Policymakers to Prioritize Addressing the Roots of Online Harm
articles.summary: Germany doxes 'UNKN,' the elusive mastermind behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware operations, revealing 31-year-old Russian Daniil Maksimovich Shchukin. The man behind 130 acts of digital sabotage finally gets his close-up.

articles.title: EFF Submission to UK Consultation on Digital ID
articles.summary: EFF channels NSA whistleblower William Binney's warning about 'turnkey totalitarian state' surveillance infrastructure. Politicians come and go, but the panopticon is forever — unless we tear it down first.

articles.title: Romance scammers turn sweet talk into £102M payday
articles.summary: ShinyHunters dumps 119K Vimeo email addresses after breaching third-party analytics vendor Anodot. Because apparently every video platform needs to share your data with companies you've never heard of.
